METHODS: This retrospective two-center real-world study included 260 intensive care unit patients from one center as the modeling cohort (randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and 91 patients from an independent center as the external validation cohort. Ten ML and deep learning algorithms were constructed using demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables. The optimal model was interpreted via Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). RESULTS: The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model achieved the most favorable point estimates. On the internal test set (n = 52): the model yielded an R2 of 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.81), RMSE of 3.22 (95% CI 2.62-3.77), MAE of 2.52 (95% CI 1.98-3.10), and ±30% prediction accuracy (P30%) of 78.8% (95% CI 67.3-88.5). On the external validation cohort (n = 91), it achieved an R2 of 0.76 (95% CI 0.69-0.80), RMSE of 3.61 (95% CI 3.08-4.14), MAE of 2.89 (95% CI 2.48-3.35), and P30% of 69.2% (95% CI 59.3-78.0). After Holm-Bonferroni correction, paired bootstrap comparisons showed XGBoost significantly outperformed 5 of 9 comparator algorithms in the internal test set and 7 of 9 in the external cohort, with performance comparable to several other tree-based ensemble methods. SHAP analysis identified daily dose, hemodialysis, and mechanical ventilation as features positively associated with predicted teicoplanin concentrations. CONCLUSION: This internally and externally validated interpretable XGBoost model delivers consistent cross-cohort performance, and serves as a dose-anchored adjunct to conventional therapeutic drug monitoring, providing a preliminary methodological foundation for exploring individualized teicoplanin dosing strategies.

articles.title: Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and modulates wnt/ β  -catenin signaling and androgen receptor conformational dynamics.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dermal papilla cells regulate hair follicle growth, yet bioactive peptides that influence both pro-growth signaling and androgen receptor (AR)-associated regulation remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effects of Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) on human dermal papilla cell function and its potential interaction with the AR ligand-binding domain (AR-LBD). METHODS: Human dermal papilla cells were treated with MT12, with bicalutamide as a pharmacological reference. Cell viability, proliferation, and expression of Wnt/ β  -catenin-related, AR-associated, and hair-growth-related genes were assessed by CCK-8, EdU incorporation, and quantitative PCR, respectively. Molecular docking, 500-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and residue communication-network analysis were used to characterize MT12-AR-LBD interactions. RESULTS: MT12 showed good cytocompatibility and significantly increased dermal papilla cell proliferation, with EdU-positive cells increasing from approximately 5% in controls to 18%-22% after treatment. MT12 increased CTNNB1 and WNT5A expression and reduced DKK1 expression, together with changes in AR, TGF- β  1, and PEDF/SERPINF1 transcripts. Computational analyses indicated that MT12 remained associated with the AR-LBD binding pocket and altered local flexibility, conformational sampling, correlated residue motions, and intradomain communication. A recurrent ASN705-MET895-ILE898 route linked the ligand-binding region to the H12/AF-2 regulatory region. DISCUSSION: MT12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and induces a Wnt/ β  -catenin-related transcriptional profile consistent with pro-growth signaling, while structural analyses suggest modulation of AR conformational dynamics. These integrated cellular and computational findings support MT12 as a potential modulator of dermal papilla cell function, although AR-related activity and the causal role of Wnt/ β  -catenin signaling require further validation.

articles.title: TACE plus systemic therapy in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma: a comparison of lenvatinib and donafenib.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) combined with systemic therapy versus TACE monotherapy in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to compare the efficacies of lenvatinib and donafenib when combined with TACE and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). METHODS: This retrospective study included 176 patients with advanced HCC receiving initial TACE, categorized into combination therapy (n = 128) or TACE monotherapy (n = 48) groups. A subgroup analysis compared TACE plus ICIs combined with lenvatinib (n = 78) or donafenib (n = 33). Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized to minimize baseline confounding variables. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. RESULTS: Combination therapy achieved a significantly higher objective treatment effective rate than monotherapy (75.0% vs. 41.7%, P < 0.001), with significantly prolonged PFS and OS, a benefit maintained after PSM. Among the specific regimens, the lenvatinib-based combination yielded a higher objective effective rate than donafenib (83.3% vs. 63.6%, P = 0.023). Post-PSM, the lenvatinib group maintained a significant PFS advantage (P = 0.007), while OS showed a marginal trend toward improvement (P = 0.057). Multivariate analysis identified treatment without combined systemic therapy and ineffective treatment response as independent predictors of inferior OS. Severe TACE-related adverse events (Grade 3/4) were comparable between combination and monotherapy cohorts (18.8% vs. 14.6%, P = 0.518), as well as between the lenvatinib and donafenib subgroups (21.8% vs. 15.2%, P = 0.422). CONCLUSION: TACE combined with systemic therapy significantly improves clinical outcomes in advanced HCC without increasing severe toxicity. Furthermore, the triple therapy of TACE, ICIs, and lenvatinib confers superior PFS and tumor response rates compared to the donafenib-based regimen, along with a trend toward OS improvement that did not reach statistical significance.

articles.title: Esculentoside A alleviates intestinal dysmotility in acute pancreatitis with potential involvement of the NF-κB/nNOS pathway in enteric neurons.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Esculentoside A (EsA), a triterpenoid saponin from Phytolacca esculenta roots, exerts anti-inflammatory, antitumor, and other pharmacological effects. However, its role in AP-related intestinal motility disorders rema1ins unexplored. The mechanism underlying intestinal dysmotility in acute pancreatitis (AP) remains unclear, with enteric neurons (ENs) playing a primary role. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of intestinal dysmotility in AP and explore the therapeutic potential of EsA intervention. METHODS: An in vivo rat model of AP was established, together with in vitro AP models using co-cultured ENs and intestinal smooth muscle cells (ISMCs), followed by EsA intervention. Differential proteins were screened via proteomics and subjected to bioinformatic analysis. Intestinal motility was evaluated by detecting the contractile activity of colonic smooth muscle strips, fecal pellet counts, as well as the contractile activity and migratory capacity of ISMCs. Nitric oxide (NO) levels were measured. Immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry were used to determine the number of nNOS-positive neurons, nNOS expression, and NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation. Western blotting was performed to detect the protein levels of PI3K/Akt/NF-κB/nNOS signaling-related molecules. RESULTS: LC-MS/MS proteomic analysis revealed significant enrichment of NF-κB and PI3K/Akt pathways in the muscularis of AP rats. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments during AP demonstrated activation of the PI3K/Akt/NF-κB/nNOS pathways, manifested by elevated p-PI3K, p-Akt, p-IKKβ, p-NF-κB p65, and p-IκBα levels, increased IκBα degradation, enhanced NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, and upregulation of nNOS expression and nNOS-positive neuronal counts, thereby promoting NO production. This inhibited the contractile activity and migratory capacity of ISMCs, ultimately reducing rat fecal pellet counts in rats and decreasing the contractile activity of colonic muscle strips. EsA intervention contributed to downregulating the nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, nNOS expression, and NO levels in ENs, thereby improving ISMC function. CONCLUSION: Aberrant activation of the PI3K/Akt/NF-κB/nNOS pathway may contribute to the pathogenesis of intestinal dysmotility in AP. EsA may reduce NO production, presumably by suppressing the NF-κB/nNOS axis, thereby ameliorating AP-associated intestinal dysmotility.

articles.title: MDM-DDI: a drug-drug interaction prediction framework integrating multi-dimensional molecular features and memory-augmented networks.
articles.abstract: When patients take multiple medications concurrently, drug-drug interactions (DDIs) can induce severe adverse reactions, making accurate DDI prediction critical for ensuring medication safety. Existing deep learning approaches often struggle to comprehensively characterize the complex molecular structures and physicochemical properties of drug molecules. Meanwhile, related studies that directly incorporate pharmacological knowledge from large language models tend to introduce redundant noise, thereby limiting predictive performance. To address these issues, we propose MDM-DDI, a framework that integrates four dimensions of drug molecular features: one-dimensional sequences, two-dimensional topologies, three-dimensional conformations, and pharmacological prior knowledge. A bidirectional drug interaction module is designed to capture latent associations between drug pairs, and a memory network mechanism is innovatively introduced to filter and denoise the pharmacological priors generated by large language models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including DrugBank demonstrate that MDM-DDI achieves small but consistent improvements over the evaluated baseline methods across multiple evaluation metrics, and also shows improvements over the evaluated baseline methods under cold-start scenarios. Case studies and interpretability analyses further provide preliminary evidence for the rationality of the model predictions.

articles.title: Tolerability, administration burden, and patient-reported experience of riluzole formulations in ALS: a longitudinal real-world study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Riluzole is available as tablets (T), oral suspension (OS), and orodispersible film (OF), but comparative real-world data on tolerability, administration burden, and patient-reported experience are limited. METHODS: In this longitudinal study, 138 patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) were evaluated at baseline (79 OF, 21 OS, 38 T) and 97 were reassessed after a median of 3.9 months. RESULTS: OS-treated patients had longer disease duration and greater functional impairment than OF or T (p < 0.001), reflecting preferential use in more advanced disease. Oral numbness was more frequent with OF than OS or T (54.4% vs. 14.3% vs. 13.2%; p < 0.001) and decreased during follow-up (42.3%-28.9%; p = 0.016), partly because patients reporting it switched away from OF. OF use (adjusted OR 10.55 vs. T, p < 0.001) and female sex (OR 2.59, p = 0.035) were independently associated with higher, and older age with lower, odds of an adverse event at baseline (OR 0.43 per 10-year increment, p < 0.001); at 3-month follow-up, OF remained the strongest formulation-related predictor (OR 5.42, p = 0.024), while an adverse event already present at baseline was itself the strongest predictor of one at follow-up (OR 5.11, p = 0.006). Dysphagia was associated with tablet manipulation (OR 7.19, p = 0.034). Differences among formulations concerned packaging convenience and independent self-administration rather than overall satisfaction, and lower disease severity was weakly associated with higher satisfaction regardless of formulation (ρ = 0.21, p = 0.015). Formulation persistence among reassessed patients was high (85.6%), and most patients who left OF had anticipated this intention at baseline. DISCUSSION: The three riluzole formulations are used in clinically distinct ALS populations and differ in tolerability and usability rather than overall satisfaction, and a prior adverse event marks persisting risk. Formulation choice should be individualized and periodically reassessed as disease progresses.

articles.title: Dose optimisation of carboplatin in the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen for HER2-Positive breast cancer: a real-world dose-response analysis using restricted cubic splines.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The docetaxel-carboplatin-trastuzumab-pertuzumab (TCbHP) regimen is widely used as a standard neoadjuvant strategy for HER2-positive breast cancer and provides substantial pathologic complete response (pCR) benefits. However, evidence on the optimal balance between treatment efficacy and toxicity remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the dose-response relationship between carboplatin exposure and pCR and to explore its association with treatment-related adverse events. METHODS: In this retrospective study, clinical data were collected from patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who received the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen followed by surgery at two tertiary hospitals between January 2019 and December 2023. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) models and Firth's bias-reduced penalized-likelihood logistic regression analyses were applied to assess the association and dose-response relationship between actual carboplatin exposure (dAUC) and pCR after adjustment for relevant confounders. RESULTS: Among 153 eligible patients, 107 (69.9%) achieved pCR. Patients with pCR had significantly higher carboplatin exposure compared with those without pCR. RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear dose-response relationship between carboplatin dAUC and pCR probability (overall trend p = 0.050; non-linearity p = 0.114), with an exploratory exposure threshold of 5.49 mg min/mL. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that higher carboplatin exposure, as measured by dAUC, was independently associated with reduced odds of achieving non-pCR. However, excessively high carboplatin exposure was significantly associated with an elevated risk of thrombocytopenia, while patients who experienced liver injury exhibited lower carboplatin exposure. CONCLUSION: Carboplatin exposure showed a linear association with pCR in patients receiving the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen. Low exploratory exposure (5.49 mg min/mL) may compromise treatment efficacy, while excessively high exposure may increase hematologic toxicity. These findings provide real-world evidence to support individualized carboplatin dosing strategies aimed at optimizing the efficacy-toxicity balance.

articles.title: Ethnobotanical survey and pharmacognostic characterization of medicinal plants traditionally used for schistosomiasis in Huambo, Angola: focus on Gladiolus dalenii and Vernonia britteniana.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In Angola, schistosomiasis remains a critical public health challenge, where traditional medicine serves as a pillar for primary healthcare. This study documents and evaluates medicinal plants used by traditional medicine practitioners (TMPs) in Huambo to treat this disease, identifying priority species for pharmacological research. METHODS: Ethnobotanical data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 23 TMPs. RESULTS: A total of 23 plant species were reported, with Gladiolus dalenii subsp. andongensis (Baker) Goldblatt and Vernonia britteniana Hiern being among the most frequently cited. Their respective subterranean organs (corm and root-tuber) are the primary parts used in traditional preparations. Macroscopic and microscopic characterizations documented a set of characteristic features, including calcium oxalate raphides in G. dalenii subsp. andongensis and sphero-crystalline structures morphologically consistent with inulin in V. britteniana, which contribute for pharmacognostic identification and quality control when interpreted together with the remaining anatomical characters. CONCLUSION: Direct anti-schistosomal evidence remains unavailable for Gladiolus dalenii subsp. andongensis, whereas Vernonia britteniana has previously shown in vitro cercaricidal activity and has undergone preliminary phytochemical characterization. However, comprehensive pharmacological and safety validation of both plant materials remains incomplete. The present findings extend the available evidence by documenting their ethnobotanical relevance and establishing preliminary macroscopic and microscopic identity features for the plant materials used in Huambo. These findings provide a preliminary pharmacognostic and ethnobotanical foundation for further evaluation of their antischistosomal potential and safety.

articles.title: Targeting STAT5 abrogates survival signaling and sensitizes chronic lymphocytic leukemia cells to BCL-2 and MCL-1 inhibition.
articles.abstract: STAT5 is constitutively activated in several hematologic malignancies, where it promotes cell survival. In chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), although STAT5b levels are elevated in leukemic cells from CLL patients compared with healthy controls, the functional significance and mechanistic role of STAT5 remains poorly understood. In this study, we knocked down both STAT5A and STAT5B using lentivirus-mediated shRNA. Loss of STAT5 significantly inhibited CLL cell viability and induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, STAT5 depletion markedly attenuated the activation of the pro-survival AKT and ERK signaling pathways and reduced the expression of the anti-apoptotic proteins MCL-1 and BCL-2, indicating that STAT5 is important for CLL cell survival and represents a potential therapeutic target. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of STAT5 with the small-molecule compound AC-4-130 significantly suppressed cell viability and promoted apoptosis in CLL cells, accompanied by diminished AKT and ERK signaling and reduced MCL-1 and BCL-2 expression. Furthermore, AC-4-130 in combination with the BCL-2 inhibitor ABT-199 or the MCL-1 inhibitor A-1210477 induced greater CLL cell apoptosis in a dose- and patient-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that STAT5 confers a survival advantage on CLL cells and that its depletion or inhibition triggers apoptosis, providing a preclinical rationale for testing STAT5 inhibitors in combination therapy for CLL.

articles.title: Abundance of carboxylesterase 1 in liver tissue and plasma-derived extracellular vesicles: Considerations for model-informed precision dosing.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Precision dosing requires accounting for variability in drug elimination capacity. Liquid biopsy, based on cell-free RNA (cfRNA) from plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), offers a minimally invasive approach to characterize hepatic enzymes. The present study extends this framework to carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), an important determinant of exposure to prodrugs and active drugs. METHODS: Matched liver tissue and plasma from 29 liver cancer patients were processed to measure CES1 protein (tissue proteomics) and cfRNA (RNA-seq of plasma-derived EVs). Individualized physiologically based pharmacokinetic models were generated to test the feasibility of model-informed precision dosing of D-methylphenidate and oseltamivir. RESULTS: CES1 cfRNA in plasma EVs (0.79 ± 0.62 reads per million [RPM]) was correlated with protein abundance in liver (942.98 ± 427.04 pmol/mg protein) from the colorectal liver metastasis cohort (Pearson's r = .57, p = .003, n = 25). Individual cfRNA measurements were projected into hepatic CES1 abundance-based dosing inputs for simulations. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the determinants of exposure variability were CES1 abundance for D-methylphenidate and renal function for oseltamivir carboxylate. Liquid biopsy-informed dosing improved precision for D-methylphenidate only modestly, with greater benefits anticipated in populations exhibiting wider CES1 expression variability (2.8-fold reduction in variability predicted over the CES1 population expression range). Renal function-based individualization fully restored precision and accuracy for oseltamivir carboxylate (1.0-fold relative to reference population exposure), compared with uniform dosing (1.6-fold). CONCLUSIONS: The findings underscore that liquid biopsy and conventional physiological markers are complementary tools within a model-informed precision dosing framework, each most valuable when applied to the rate-limiting elimination pathway.

articles.title: Concomitant use of oral second-generation integrase inhibitors and enzyme-inducing drugs: Clinical outcomes from a real-world case series.
articles.abstract: Dolutegravir (DTG) and bictegravir (BIC) are preferred antiretroviral agents, but clinical data on their concomitant use with enzyme-inducing medications remain limited. We reviewed clinical cases published on clinicalcasesDDIs.com (2019-2026) involving dolutegravir or bictegravir and potentially inducing medications. Twenty-six cases were identified: 15 involved BIC and 11 dolutegravir. Concomitant medications included antiepileptic drugs (n = 13), rifamycins (n = 6), anticancer agents (n = 3), over-the-counter products (n = 3) and ursodeoxycholic acid (n = 1). Liverpool classifications were 'do not coadminister' in 12 cases (46.2%), 11 (42.3%) potential interactions, two (7.7%) potential weak interactions and one (3.8%) no interaction expected. Integrase inhibitor (INSTI) dose adjustment to twice-daily dosing occurred in five cases, and therapeutic drug monitoring was used in six. Virological suppression was maintained or achieved in all five dose-adjusted cases (100%) and in 19 of 21 cases without adjustment (90.5%). The remaining two cases (9.5%) involved isolated episodes of transient viraemia after prior suppression during standard-dose BIC/FTC/TAF coadministration with St John's wort or carbamazepine. Both resuppressed after withdrawal of the interacting product without changing antiretroviral therapy; neither episode established confirmed virological failure. These selected reports highlight the importance of reviewing concomitant medications and monitoring virological outcomes during coadministration of second-generation INSTI and enzyme-inducing drugs.

articles.title: Nanoemulsion adjuvant induces functional immunity to group A Streptococcus vaccines.
articles.abstract: Peptide-based vaccines offer a safe and chemically defined alternative to traditional whole-pathogen vaccines, but short peptide antigens typically generate weak immune responses and therefore require effective adjuvant systems. Group A Streptococcus (GAS) causes significant throat and skin infections worldwide, and their serious post-infectious complications contribute to a major global health burden, yet no vaccines currently exist to prevent or treat these infections. To address this limitation, we designed and evaluated two adjuvant systems designed to enhance the immunogenicity of the GAS peptide antigen, J8: (1) physically mixed adjuvant vaccines incorporating cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) and a TLR-2-activating lipopeptide, and (2) a nanoemulsion adjuvant system capable of co-delivering the antigen with CPPs. Both systems were formulated into nanoparticles, characterised, and then assessed in vivo following subcutaneous immunisation in mice. While each approach improved J8-specific antibody responses compared with the GAS antigen alone, the nanoemulsion-based vaccines elicited markedly higher IgG titres, a more balanced Th1/Th2 profile, and stronger opsonic activity against multiple GAS clinical isolates. Longitudinal serum analysis demonstrated that the simple nanoemulsion adjuvanted vaccines generated durable antibody responses comparable to, or exceeding, clinically approved MF59 adjuvant. This work highlights the potential of nanoemulsion-based technologies to advance the development of synthetic peptide vaccines requiring strong and long-lasting immunity.

articles.title: Propofol rapidly reverses cognitive impairments with restoration of sleep stability and alleviation of neuroinflammation in sleep-deprived mice.
articles.abstract: Acute total sleep deprivation (SD) produces immediate and severe cognitive impairments. Although propofol has been shown to be effective against cognitive impairments under certain SD circumstances, its pharmacological profile under acute total SD remains to be further explored. The present study found that a single subanesthetic bolus of propofol (35-50 mg/kg, i.p.) rapidly ameliorated acute total SD-induced cognitive impairments, with effects observed as early as one hour after administration and persisting for 24 hours in the Y-maze test, whereas the classical hypnotic zolpidem (ZPD, 1.25-5 mg/kg) was ineffective in rescuing cognition. Propofol's cognitive-improving effect was also demonstrated in novel object recognition and object location recognition tasks. Meanwhile, non-invasive sleep monitoring revealed that propofol increased the proportions of medium-to-long duration non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep (64-128 seconds), and reduced the episode numbers of short-duration NREM sleep (0-4, 4-8, and 8-16 seconds) in SD mice. EEG/EMG recordings confirmed that propofol increased total NREM duration by prolonging mean episode duration. In contrast, ZPD failed to reverse NREM sleep fragmentation under either monitoring modality, although it did prolong total NREM sleep duration. Moreover, propofol upregulated the core circadian regulator BMAL1, reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and TNF-α), restored the expression of key neuroplasticity-related proteins (BDNF, PSD-95, and SYN), and reversed SD-induced loss of dendritic spines in the hippocampus. Together, these findings suggest that propofol rapidly ameliorates SD-induced cognitive impairments, and that this behavioral rescue is associated with the restoration of sleep stability and attenuation of neuroinflammation.

articles.title: NDUFA7 targeting by Tanshinone IIA mitigates ischemic injury in cardiomyocytes: A mechanism of restoring mitochondrial complex I activity in myocardial ischemia.
articles.abstract: Tanshinone IIA (Tan IIA) is an active component of Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (Danshen). Although Tan IIA exerts cardioprotective effects in cardiovascular diseases and its formulation, sodium tanshinone IIA sulfonate, treats ischemic heart disease, its direct molecular targets and mechanisms against myocardial ischemia (MI) remain unknown. This study aimed to identify mechanisms of Tan IIA against MI, focusing on NDUFA7 as a direct target, using in vitro and in vivo models. An ISO-induced MI mouse model was established to evaluate cardioprotective effects using electrocardiogram, histopathological changes, biochemical markers, oxidative stress, immunofluorescence, and western blot. Potential targets were identified by isothermal shift assay (iTSA) and validated using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), drug affinity-responsive target stability (DARTS), and bio-layer interferometry (BLI). In vitro, a tert-butyl hydroperoxide-induced AC16 cardiomyocyte injury model assessed cell viability, mitochondrial ROS, and complex I activity, with shRNA-mediated knockdown for validation. In MI mice, Tan IIA pretreatment (5/10 mg/kg) ameliorated ECG abnormalities, improved histopathological injury, attenuated myocardial fibrosis, decreased serum cardiac injury biomarkers, and enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities. iTSA identified NDUFA7, a critical subunit of mitochondrial respiratory complex I, as a potential Tan IIA target, confirmed by docking, MD simulations, CETSA, DARTS, and BLI. In vitro, Tan IIA improved cell viability, suppressed mitochondrial ROS, restored complex I activity, and enhanced NDUFA7-MCM3 interaction. NDUFA7 knockdown abolished these protective effects. This study identifies NDUFA7 as a target of Tan IIA that restores mitochondrial complex I activity against MI, highlighting it as anti-MI drug screening.

articles.title: Comparison of anti-hyperuricemic activity of berberine and metformin: Insight from de novo purine biosynthesis and purine metabolism and intestinal microbiome.
articles.abstract: Increasing evidence has shown that the worldwide epidemic of metabolic disease including hyperuricemia (HUA) correlates with an elevation in serum uric acid (UA) as well as a marked increase in total fructose intake. Phellodendri Chinensis Cortex (PC) is a traditional medicinal material used to treat metabolic diseases including gout and HUA. Berberine (BBR), the main component of PC, possesses anti-HUA and anti-gout effects. Metformin is widely used for the treatment of metabolic syndrome. However, their effect on HUA induced by high-fructose remained unexplored. The present work endeavored to explore the anti-HUA potential of BBR and metformin on high-fructose-induced hyperuricemic rats focusing on intestinal microbiota, de novo purine biosynthesis (DNPB) of endogenous purine, purine cycle and metabolism and intestinal microbiota. Results indicated that BBR and metformin remarkably decreased the high levels of UA, creatinine, and urea induced by a long-term high-fructose diet. BBR and metformin activated the expression of ketohexokinase (KHK) and suppressed the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) to regulate fructose metabolism. Following that, BBR and metformin suppressed the activated DNPB induced by high-fructose, through which a great number of purine synthesis was inhibited. Besides, BBR promoted the purine salvage pathway (PSP) and suppressed the expression of xanthine oxidase (XOD) to inhibit the purine metabolism, resulting in the increase of inosine and decrease of IMP, hypoxanthine and xanthine, and accelerating the purine cycle. Metformin decreased the levels of inosine, IMP, hypoxanthine and xanthine, inhibiting purine cycle and metabolism. Additionally, BBR and metformin favorably modulated the species of gut microbiota, regulated intestinal purine absorption and excretion, decreased the intestinal purine contents and increased the fecal uricase and allantoinase concentration to recover UA catabolism. Our study revealed that BBR and metformin had outstanding anti-HUA effect, which was intimately associated with suppression of PPP, DNPB and XOD in the liver and modulation of the intestinal microbiota. BBR and metformin deserved to provide a preclinical basis for further investigation for the treatment of HUA.

articles.title: Vonoprazan Protects Against Methotrexate-Induced Testicular Toxicity by Attenuating Oxidative Stress, ER Stress, NLRP3/IL-1β Inflammation, and Apoptosis in Mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Methotrexate (MTX) is widely used for malignant and inflammatory disorders but may cause male reproductive toxicity through oxidative stress, inflammation, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, hormonal suppression, and testicular injury. This study evaluated the protective effects of vonoprazan against MTX-induced testicular toxicity in mice. METHODS: Adult male Swiss albino mice were divided into five groups (n=6): normal control, vonoprazan control, MTX, low-dose vonoprazan + MTX, and high-dose vonoprazan + MTX. Vonoprazan was administered orally at 50 or 100 mg/kg/day, and MTX intraperitoneally at 10 mg/kg. Serum testosterone, epididymal sperm count, oxidative/antioxidant markers, ER stress and inflammatory markers, testicular histopathology, and active Caspase-1 and B-cell lymphoma 2-associated X protein (Bax) immunohistochemistry were assessed. RESULTS: MTX significantly reduced serum testosterone, epididymal sperm count, reduced glutathione (GSH), and total antioxidant capacity (TAC), while increasing malondialdehyde (MDA), PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP signaling, NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) levels (p<0.05). Vonoprazan, particularly at 100 mg/kg, significantly attenuated these alterations compared with MTX (p<0.05). Histopathological examination revealed severe seminiferous tubular degeneration following MTX administration, with marked restoration after high-dose vonoprazan. Active Caspase-1 and Bax immunoreactivity was markedly increased by MTX and progressively reduced by vonoprazan. CONCLUSION: Vonoprazan mitigated MTX-induced testicular injury by restoring antioxidant defenses, reducing lipid peroxidation, suppressing ER stress and NLRP3/IL-1β signaling, attenuating apoptosis and inflammasome activation, and preserving testicular structure and function.

articles.title: CEBPD promotes smooth muscle cell phenotypic transition and aortic wall degeneration in aortic dissection.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic transition and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling contribute to aortic wall degeneration in aortic dissection (AD). We aimed to identify transcriptional regulators associated with ECM-remodeling SMC states and investigate their contribution to AD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Human and mouse transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility datasets were integrated to identify candidate regulators. Validation included human aortic tissue analysis and gain- and loss-of-function studies in human aortic SMCs and a β-aminopropionitrile (BAPN)-induced mouse model. Functional assays, histological assessment, chromatin immunoprecipitation-qPCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed. KEY FINDINGS: Synthetic-like SMC populations expanded in AD and displayed reduced contractile signatures and enhanced ECM-remodeling features. CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein delta (CEBPD) was upregulated and showed increased inferred regulatory activity across human and mouse datasets. Tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) induced CEBPD expression in SMCs. CEBPD overexpression reduced contractile marker expression and impaired contractility, whereas knockdown partially attenuated TNF-α-induced phenotypic changes. Chromatin accessibility analysis identified candidate targets enriched in processes related to SMC proliferation and differentiation, inflammation, and tissue remodeling. Matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP2) was validated as a direct transcriptional target. In vivo, CEBPD overexpression aggravated BAPN-induced aortic dilation, medial degeneration, elastin fragmentation, and SMC phenotypic changes, whereas knockdown attenuated these effects. SIGNIFICANCE: CEBPD promotes SMC phenotypic transition and contributes to aortic wall degeneration. These findings support its involvement in ECM remodeling, with MMP2 representing one validated target within a broader candidate gene set.

articles.title: Therapeutic Effects of Low-Frequency Renal Nerve Neuromodulation in a Preclinical Model of Obesity-Induced Hypertension.
articles.abstract: Obesity-associated hypertension is increasingly prevalent and often resistant to pharmacological treatment. The renal nerve is a promising target for neuromodulation due to its critical role in blood pressure (BP) regulation. This study investigated the efficacy and physiological impact of low-frequency renal nerve stimulation (RNS) in Zucker fatty rats (ZFRs), a preclinical model of obesity-induced hypertension. Thirteen anesthetized male ZFRs underwent surgical implantation of bipolar stimulating electrodes on the left renal nerve. RNS was applied at 2.5 Hz and 5.0 Hz (0.5 mA, 0.5 ms, 30 s) while continuously recording mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate (HR), hindquarter flow (HQF), and ipsilateral and contralateral renal cortical perfusion (RCP). Hindquarter resistance (HQR) and renal cortical resistance (RCR) were calculated from MAP and corresponding flow values. Baseline MAP was 115 ± 5 mmHg. RNS at both frequencies produced immediate reductions in MAP (2.5 Hz: 29 ± 6 mmHg; 5.0 Hz: 30 ± 6 mmHg) without significant changes in HR. Both frequencies similarly increased HQF, with a corresponding decrease in HQR. Ipsilateral RCP was reduced at both frequencies, with a greater decrease observed at 5.0 Hz. RCR was reduced to a similar extent on both sides, with contralateral RCP significantly reduced only at 2.5 Hz. Low-frequency RNS effectively lowers BP in ZFRs possibly via reflex-mediated vasodilation. Reductions in renal vascular resistance despite reduced flow likely reflect compensatory renal vasodilation. Importantly, the 2.5 Hz protocol achieved similar BP-lowering effects with a smaller impact on renal perfusion, supporting its potential as a safer neuromodulatory strategy in obesity-related hypertension.

articles.title: Aurantii Fructus produces rapid antidepressant effects by suppressing the hippocampal non-canonical Caspase-4/NLRP3 inflammasome.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Aurantii Fructus (AF), the dried immature fruit of Citrus aurantium L. (Rutaceae), is a classical qi-regulating traditional Chinese medicine and a key constituent of prescriptions traditionally used for liver qi stagnation with depressive mood. This documented traditional use provides the rationale for investigating its antidepressant potential. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study evaluated the rapid antidepressant potential of AF and elucidated its hippocampal mechanism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: HPLC fingerprinting ensured chemical consistency across batches. C57BL/6J mice subjected to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) received a single dose of AF (2 or 4 g/kg) or ketamine, followed by behavioral testing. Hippocampal transcriptomic profiling was performed in CUMS mice to identify molecular targets, and causal involvement of Caspase-4 (mouse caspase-11, orthologous to human caspase-4) was validated by adeno-associated virus-mediated hippocampal overexpression in naive mice. RESULTS: HPLC confirmed batch reproducibility (RSD < 5%), with narirutin, hesperidin, neohesperidin, and nobiletin as the principal flavonoids. AF at 4 g/kg ameliorated CUMS-induced despair in the 2-h tail suspension and 12-h forced swimming tests and restored sucrose preference at 24 h without altering locomotor activity. Transcriptomic profiling identified hippocampal Caspase-4/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling as a core stress signature that AF markedly attenuated. Caspase-4 overexpression blocked the despair-relieving effects of AF in naive mice, and blocked AF's effects on decreasing NLRP3, NF-κB p65, GBP1, and IBA-1 expression, and increasing CaMKII, PSD95, and synapsin 1. CONCLUSIONS: AF produces rapid antidepressant-like effects by suppressing the hippocampal non-canonical Caspase-4 (Casp4/caspase-11)/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, supporting its ethnopharmacological application in depression.

articles.title: Tibetan medicine Shiwei Dida capsule alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: involvement of fatty acid metabolism regulation and IRE1α/XBP1s pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Shiwei Dida capsule (, SWD) is a classical Tibetan medicinal formula originating from the canonical Tibetan medical text The Four Tantras, and has been employed in Tibetan medicine for more than a millennium. The Drug Standards of the Ministry of Health of the People's Republic of China (Tibetan Medicine) explicitly state that SWD possesses the effects of soothing the liver and regulating qi flow, clearing heat and detoxifying, and benefiting the gallbladder to dissolve calculi. The formula is indicated for re-yuan-xing mkhris pa (Chiba), a condition corresponding to febrile hepatobiliary diseases in Tibetan medicine theory. The traditional use of SWD provides an ethnopharmacological basis for investigating its effects in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). However, its bioactive components and underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: By combining metabolomics, proteomics, and molecular biology, this study methodically investigated the effectiveness of SWD and its molecular mechanisms against MASH. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical components of SWD were analysed both qualitatively and quantitatively using UHPLC. Western diet (WD)-induced mice were used as an in vivo MASH model, while palmitic acid (PA)-stimulated AML12 cells were employed as an in vitro model of hepatocyte lipotoxicity and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. SWD and SWD-containing serum were used for intervention in the respective models. Untargeted metabolomics identified SWD-modulated metabolites. Quantitative proteomics identified the potential target proteins of SWD. The underlying molecular pathways were then predicted using a bioinformatics enrichment study. Molecular pathways predicted were validated through immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, and RT-qPCR analyses. Blood constituents of SWD were identified through UPLC-Q Exactive Orbitrap-MS analysis. High-throughput screening for absorbed components was conducted by establishing a stable XBP1-mNeonGreen HEK293T cell line. Cellular thermal shift assay, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation were utilised to explore the potential interactions with, and cellular engagement of, the target by these preliminary bioactive compounds. The molecular mechanism underlying the hepatoprotective effect of SWD was further investigated by XBP1s overexpression. RESULTS: SWD improved MASH symptoms, including hepatic steatosis, liver function indices, inflammatory response, oxidative stress, and glycometabolism in WD-fed mice. SWD-containing serum reduced lipid accumulation, inflammation, and oxidative stress in PA-induced AML12 and HepG2 cells. Exploratory metabolomics suggested that SWD rescued candidate metabolites enriched in fatty acid metabolism-related pathways. Exploratory proteomics further suggested that the IRE1α/XBP1s pathway was a potential mechanistic candidate underlying SWD's hepatoprotective effects. Additionally, 54 prototype components absorbed into blood were identified, with swertiamarin, gentiopicroside, sweroside, protopine, and taurochenodeoxycholic acid emerging as preliminary candidate compounds that inhibit the XBP1s-mNeonGreen reporter activity in the primary screening assay. Mechanistically, SWD regulated SREBP-1c-mediated fatty acid metabolism to restore hepatic lipid homeostasis and was associated with modulation of IRE1α/XBP1s signaling, which may contribute to the alleviation of ER stress and autophagy dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS: SWD treatment effectively protected against MASH. Its effects involved suppressing de novo lipogenesis, improving hepatic lipid homeostasis, and modulating ER stress and autophagy. IRE1α/XBP1s signaling was identified as a candidate contributing pathway, but its necessity and causal role remained to be established. This study offers a novel perspective on the Tibetan medicine system's approach to the treatment of MASH and provides preclinical evidence supporting the therapeutic potential of SWD against MASH.

articles.title: System-level Mapping of the Anti-Inflammatory Mechanisms of Curcumin Through Convergent Network Pharmacology, Single-Cell Transcriptomics, and Gut Microbiome Multi-Omics: A Systems Biology Approach.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Curcumin, the primary bioactive polyphenol derived from Curcuma longa L. (Jianghuang), has been utilized in Traditional Chinese Medicine for over two millennia to resolve blood stasis and manage inflammatory conditions. Historical texts, including the Tang Materia Medica (659 AD) and the Compendium of Materia Medica (1596 AD), document its systemic efficacy in treating "masses" and arthritic syndromes, aligning with modern chronic inflammatory pathologies. AIM OF THE STUDY: Despite its therapeutic promise, curcumin exhibits a "bioavailability paradox", characterized by potent pharmacological effects despite poor oral absorption. This study aimed to systematically investigate the potential anti-inflammatory mechanisms of curcumin across seven major inflammation-associated diseases and explore the contribution of gut microbiota-mediated systemic regulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A convergent systems biology pipeline integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate potential interactions between curcumin and inflammatory targets. Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from seven disease models (RA, DM, AS, IBD, AD, CRC, and PsO) were reanalyzed using AUCell scoring to prioritize drug-responsive cellular niches. A microbe-metabolite-target multi-omics network was constructed using gutMGene and GMrepo. In vivo validation was performed using curcumin-treated mice with or without antibiotic depletion, combined with serum metabolite profiling by UPLC-HRMS, 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted and targeted metabolomics, and fecal supernatant (FS) bioassays in LPS-stimulated macrophages. Additional molecular docking and cellular experiments were conducted to investigate the potential target interactions and anti-inflammatory activities of tetrahydrocurcumin (THC). RESULTS: Global analysis identified three interconnected regulatory axes associated with curcumin: (1) an immuno-inflammatory axis (RA, IBD, PsO) involving TNF, IL-6, and IL-1β; (2) a metabolic-inflammatory axis (DM, AS) involving APOE and INS; and (3) a cellular homeostasis axis (CRC, AD) involving TP53 and PRKN. Molecular docking and MD simulations provided exploratory insights into potential target interactions. Single-cell mapping revealed context-dependent cellular selectivity, identifying synovial fibroblasts and plasma cells in RA, T cells in AS, epithelial carcinoma cells in CRC, and microglia in AD as candidate responsive cellular populations. Serum metabolite profiling indicated minimal systemic exposure to parent curcumin (RSD = 65.0%), while THC showed a higher MS signal than parent curcumin. Additional docking and cellular experiments suggested potential THC-target interactions and demonstrated its anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-stimulated macrophages. Notably, high-dose curcumin enriched Akkermansia and increased butyrate levels. FS from curcumin-treated donors dose-dependently suppressed IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β secretion, an effect attenuated by antibiotic pretreatment and partially recapitulated by sodium butyrate. Furthermore, FFAR2 knockdown attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of sodium butyrate and FS-Cur-H, supporting the involvement of FFAR2-associated signaling. Multi-omics analysis further revealed associations linking Akkermansia, butyrate, FFAR2, and inflammatory regulatory networks. CONCLUSIONS: Curcumin acts as a convergent circuit regulator that bridges potential molecular interactions with gut ecological remodeling. Its anti-inflammatory effects are associated with gut microbiota-related changes and supported by the anti-inflammatory activity of fecal supernatants. This study provides a mechanistic framework that offers a potential explanation for the bioavailability paradox and substantiates the scientific connotation of the traditional "multi-disease, one-drug" therapy.

articles.title: Hydrogel-forming microneedle sampling of dermal interstitial fluid for exploratory bioequivalence assessment of topical salicylic acid ointments.
articles.abstract: Methods for characterizing local drug exposure are needed to support the development of topical semisolid products. Gantrez S-97/PEG 10,000 hydrogel-forming microneedles (HFMs) were prepared to evaluate their feasibility for local sampling and formulation comparison after topical dosing. The sampling conditions selected in rats comprised skin cleaning with 5 % sodium dodecyl sulfate followed by wiping with purified water, a needle height of approximately 800 μm and 2 cm spacing between dosing-area edges. Three 5 % (w/w) salicylic acid ointments were compared by in vitro permeation testing (IVPT), rat dermal microdialysis and HFM sampling: a marketed product used as the study reference (R), another marketed product (T1) and a laboratory formulation developed with R as the target (T2). IVPT endpoints were cumulative permeation at 48 h and maximum flux; both in vivo methods assessed peak concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration-time curve (AUC). For each method, exploratory equivalence required the 90 % confidence intervals for the test/reference geometric mean ratios of both endpoints to lie entirely within 80.00 %-125.00 %. All six T2/R intervals were within this range, with ratios of 94.58 %-106.29 %, whereas none of the six T1/R intervals were fully contained. Both in vivo methods showed a lower and later mean peak for T1 than for R, and all three methods yielded consistent comparison outcomes. These findings suggest that HFM sampling could provide in vivo local exposure information for formulation screening and support further development of local bioequivalence assessment methods.

articles.title: CaCO3-loaded hydrogels with internal pH modulation for enhanced preservation of therapeutic enzyme activity under simulated intestinal conditions.
articles.abstract: Oral delivery of biologics remains challenging because gastrointestinal conditions can rapidly compromise therapeutic stability and activity. While enteric coatings provide protection during gastric transit, they provide limited control over the local microenvironment experienced following release. Here, a microenvironment engineering strategy is introduced based on calcium carbonate (CaCO3)-containing hydrogels, designed to complement enteric capsules by actively regulating internal pH to preserve enzymatic function under intestinal conditions. A pyranine-based ratiometric fluorescence method was developed and validated to directly quantify intragel pH and guide formulation optimization. CaCO3 incorporation generated a sustained increase in internal pH across various buffer systems (pH 5-8) and biorelevant intestinal media while minimally affecting the surrounding environment. Using phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL) as a model therapeutic enzyme, it was shown that local pH regulation significantly enhanced enzymatic activity under acidic and simulated intestinal conditions. Notably, PAL-loaded CaCO3 hydrogels retained activity after transient exposure to pH 6.5 at levels comparable to those observed under continuous exposure to favorable pH 7.4 conditions. These findings establish CaCO3-based intragel pH modulation as a straightforward strategy for protecting orally delivered enzymes from physiologically relevant pH fluctuations following enteric release and provide a framework for further development of advanced oral biologic delivery systems.

articles.title: Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 fusion protein restores immune homeostasis by reducing pathogenic plasma cells in lupus nephritis.
articles.abstract: The short half-life of interleukin-2 (IL-2) and its role in broad immune-cell activation limit its therapeutic use in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). We developed Anti-FcRn-mIL-2, a bifunctional fusion protein linking a receptor-biased IL-2 mutein to a monoclonal antibody against the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), to combine cellular immune regulation with IgG homeostasis modulation. Compared with wild-type IL-2, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 exhibited greater thermal and plasma stability. In mice, it had a longer apparent half-life after subcutaneous administration and generated stronger renal fluorescence signals when labelled. In murine assays, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 induced less conventional T-cell activation than wild-type IL-2. In peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from patients with SLE, treatment with Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 reduced B-cell responses and plasma-cell frequencies. In MRL/lpr mice, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 treatment increased regulatory T-cell frequencies, reduced splenic plasma-cell frequencies, and lowered circulating IgG and anti-double-stranded DNA antibody levels. It also reduced renal IgG and complement C3 deposition and alleviated both proteinuria and renal histological injury. Under the regimens tested, Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 produced greater improvements in renal and humoral immune outcomes than coadministration of mIL-2 and Anti-FcRn. These findings demonstrate the immunomodulatory and IgG-lowering effects of Anti-FcRn-mIL-2 in MRL/lpr mice and support further preclinical evaluation for lupus nephritis.

articles.title: The pharmacogenetics of spironolactone in neonates and infants with heart disease.
articles.abstract: Spironolactone is a diuretic commonly used to treat fluid overload in neonates and infants with cardiac disease. However, there is conflicting evidence on its efficacy. Pharmacogenetics has been used in adults to predict drug response and tailor drug dosing, with evidence suggesting associations between genetic variants and spironolactone response. This study aims to evaluate the association between candidate pharmacogenetics variants and spironolactone response in neonates and infants. This is a retrospective cohort study conducted in 63 neonates and infants with cardiac conditions who had their first spironolactone exposure (FSE) at less than 30 months of age. Multivariate linear regression was performed between NR3C2 rs2070951, NR3C2 rs5522, CYP11B2 rs1799998, and spironolactone response measured by change in urine output 24 hours before FSE and 24 hours after FSE (24-hour urine response) and 72 hours after FSE (72-hour urine response). Patients with CYP11B2 rs1799998 G/G genotype had a significantly (P = .03) lower 24-hour urine response compared with A/A+A/G by 32.4 mL/kg/day. The same trend was also observed for 72-hour urine response but non-significant (P = .5). No consistent trend was observed between 24-hour urine response and 72-hour urine response for NR3C3 rs2070951 and NR3C2 rs5522.Patients with CYP11B2 rs1799998 G/G showed a significantly lower 24-hour urine response compared with A/A+A/G, demonstrating that patients with G/G genotype were the poor responders to spironolactone. With further validation studies, this variant may help elucidate mechanisms underlying variability in spironolactone response and could support future investigation into pharmacogenetic-guided dosing strategies. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This pharmacogenetic study in neonates and infants with heart disease evaluated candidate variants previously associated with spironolactone response. Neonates and infants with the CYP11B2 rs1799998 G/G genotype showed a reduced diuretic response to spironolactone compared with A/A or A/G genotypes, a biologically plausible effect given the relatively increased CYP11B2 expression in early life. With further validation studies, this variant and others may help explain variability in spironolactone response and guide dosing strategies in clinical practice.

articles.title: Propolis loaded nanogel: A targeted approach to mitigate CB1/SIRT1/HMGB1 signaling in gamma radiation-induced lung damage.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis is a disease-refractive lung condition that may develop after radiotherapy. Propolis (Prop), a natural bee resin, has a potential for managing lung diseases; however, its low bioavailability might restrict its clinical use. Accordingly, we synthesized and characterized poly(methacrylic acid) and sodium alginate (PMAA-NaAlg) nanogel using γ radiation. This study also aimed to shed more light on the principal mechanism of Prop-PMAA-NaAlg in alleviating the acute lung injury induced by ionizing radiation (IR) in vivo. The formulated Prop-PMAA-NaAlg nanogel demonstrated a minimal particle size and the highest zeta potential. Male mice were divided into 4 groups (control, [6 Gy] irradiated [IR], [50 mg/kg] IR + Prop, and IR + Prop-nanogel). The results indicated that Prop successfully loaded onto PMAA-NaAlg nanogels significantly attenuated IR-induced lung injury and improved tissue alterations. In mechanism, Prop-PMAA-NaAlg nanogels restored the cannabinoid receptor 1, high mobility group box 1, transforming growth factor-β1, and SMAD family member 3 levels to effectively inhibit the pulmonary inflammatory response; and prevented IR-induced oxidative stress by increasing the silent information regulator 1 level and stimulating the synthesis of several antioxidant enzymes. It reduced lipid peroxidation (malondialdehyde) and reactive oxygen species levels. These findings suggest that Prop-PMAA-NaAlg nanogel may exert protective effects against acute radiation-induced lung injury, potentially through modulation of the cannabinoid receptor 1/silent information regulator 1/high mobility group box 1 and transforming growth factor-β1/SMAD family member 3 signaling pathways. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study highlights a novel propolis-loaded poly(methacrylic acid)/sodium alginate (Prop-PMAA-NaAlg) nanogel synthesized using γ radiation; the formulation was evaluated for its protective potential against radiation-induced lung injury and its ability to improve Prop bioavailability. Prop-PMAA-NaAlg reduced fibrotic and oxidative stress markers, including transforming growth factor-β1, SMAD family member 3, malondialdehyde, and reactive oxygen species, while modulating the cannabinoid receptor 1/silent information regulator 1/high mobility group box 1 signaling axis, supporting its potential as a nanogel-based strategy for mitigating radiation-induced lung damage.

articles.title: Hepatocyte-based models for cytochrome P450 fraction metabolized determination: Recommendations from the Quantitative Fraction Metabolized Working Group of the International Consortium for Innovation and Quality in Pharmaceutical Development.
articles.abstract: Accurate quantification of fraction metabolized (fm) by drug metabolizing enzymes is essential for understanding clearance mechanisms, predicting interindividual variability, and assessing victim drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk during drug discovery and development. Particularly, determining fm for metabolically stable, low turnover compounds remains challenging. Traditional in vitro systems-such as human liver microsomes, hepatocyte suspensions, and recombinant enzymes-often lack the ability for extended incubation to detect parent depletion of low turnover compounds, resulting in inaccurate clearance measurement and DDI predictions. Advances including hepatocyte relay methods, cocultured hepatocyte systems (HepatoPac and HuREL), and 3-dimensional spheroid cultures, enable prolonged incubations for low turnover compounds. However, the absence of systematic cross-platform evaluations, uncertainties regarding inhibitor selectivity and stability, and variability in long-term culture performance continue to limit confidence in fm estimation. To investigate these gaps, the International Consortium for Innovation and Quality in Pharmaceutical Development established the Quantitative Fraction Metabolized Working Group to evaluate long-term in vitro platforms for fm determination. Substrates with well characterized human absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion profiles and selective cytochrome P450 (P450) inhibitors with minimal induction or cytotoxicity were selected to evaluate in inhibition studies across four systems: HepatoPac, HuREL, Spheroid, and Relay. Summarized are the results of these comparative studies, highlighting system performance, fm estimates, and methodological considerations and challenges. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that reliable application of long-term hepatocyte systems for reaction phenotyping and translation to clinical DDI prediction requires additional characterization of substrate kinetics, inhibitor potency and selectivity, induction potential, and metabolic pathway representation within each model system. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study evaluated chemical inhibitors of 7 major hepatic P450 enzymes in long-term culture (HepatoPac, HuREL, Spheroid) and Relay suspension hepatocyte systems and show differences in intrinsic clearance, inhibitor response, and fraction metabolized predictions across hepatocyte systems. While some P450 inhibitors successfully identified the known major metabolic pathways of low-turnover drugs, platform-specific factors, including differences in metabolite representation, inhibitor behavior, and effective inhibitor exposure may influence fm predictions, highlighting the need for careful qualification of these systems prior to application in reaction phenotyping.

articles.title: Guanxinning tablet attenuates carotid artery stenosis in Tibetan minipigs induced by a high-fat diet.
articles.abstract: Carotid artery stenosis (CAS), a progressive narrowing of the carotid artery primarily driven by atherosclerosis, is a major risk factor for ischemic stroke. Guanxinning tablet (GXN), a well-established traditional Chinese medicine formula, is widely used in cardiovascular diseases; however, its therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms against CAS remain largely unexplored. This study aims to investigate the effects of GXN on CAS and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. An accelerated CAS model was established using a high-fat diet (HFD) combined with left common carotid artery balloon injury in Tibetan miniature pigs. After 10 weeks of GXN administration, we evaluated systemic blood lipid profiles, carotid plaque burden via ultrasonography and arteriography, and serum biomarkers reflecting inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial injury. Comprehensive histopathological examinations (including H&E, Oil Red O, Masson's trichrome, EVG, and immunohistochemical stainings) of carotid tissues were subsequently performed. The results demonstrated that GXN significantly reduced cholesterol levels, attenuated carotid plaque area, and mitigated the severity of atherosclerotic lesions. Furthermore, GXN decreased lipid deposition and collagen accumulation while inhibiting vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) migration and intimal hyperplasia. Mechanistically, GXN suppressed oxidative stress and downregulated the expression of NF-κB, MMP-9, ICAM-1, and intimal α-SMA, thereby alleviating the inflammatory response and contributing to plaque stabilization. In summary, GXN ameliorates CAS by improving lipid metabolism, suppressing oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and inhibiting VSMC proliferation and neointimal hyperplasia, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic agent for CAS.

articles.title: Global reporting of Brugada syndrome in VigiBase®: A disproportionality analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Brugada syndrome (BrS) represents a rare but potentially malignant cardiac channelopathy, which may be precipitated by drugs, although data mainly derive from case reports/series. OBJECTIVE: To describe the global reporting of BrS with drugs, including co-occurrence patterns, and identify novel potential associations. METHODS: We used VigiBase® to perform descriptive and disproportionality analyses. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian information component (IC) with relevant 95% confidence/credibility intervals (95% CI) were used as disproportionality measures to identify signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR). We performed a network analysis to assess the co-occurrence patterns of related medications based on Jaccard similarity. RESULTS: We included 544 deduplicated cases of BrS (94.7% serious events, 30.9% females, median time to onset of 30 days, 40.8% physician-reported, 63% from North America), with bupropion (n = 50), nortriptyline (n = 40) and flecainide (n = 34) as most frequently reported suspected drugs. Among 39 drugs with at least four reports, 32 emerged with an SDR, of which 17 were not listed in the BrS website (http://www.brugadadrugs.org), such as clozapine and loperamide (often overdosed). The co-occurrence network included 17 medications, regardless of the labelled role (suspected, interacting or concomitant), with a total of 12 potential co-occurrences; fentanyl exhibited the highest closeness centrality (1.0), whereas the strongest co-occurrence was reported between bupropion and nortriptyline (Jaccard similarity of 0.31). CONCLUSIONS: Notwithstanding limitations related to pharmacovigilance and the complex BrS pathophysiology, we identified 32 medications with over-reporting of BrS, including 17 drugs not listed in the BrS website as well as clusters in affective disorders and anaesthesia.

articles.title: Assessing predictive performance of four semi-mechanistic models for long-term HbA1c with dulaglutide in people with Type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: AIM: Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) reflects the long-term glycemic control over at least 3 months in Type 2 diabetes. Predicting HbA1c using glucose data from studies of less than 3 months would be valuable. We previously evaluated four semi-mechanistic HbA1c models (ADOPT, FFH, FHH and IGRH) for their ability to predict HbA1c for the small molecule LY2409021, and the transit compartment models (FHH and IGRH) performed well. This work aims to evaluate HbA1c predictive performance of the four models for a long-acting therapeutic protein, dulaglutide. METHODS: The models were developed using dulaglutide concentrations, glucose and HbA1c data from a 5-week Phase 1b study. Model predictive performance was assessed by comparing model-estimated and observed HbA1c values from two Phase 2 and 3 studies. There were three metrics for predictive performance: (a) mean change from baseline HbA1c (ΔHbA1c) between observed and model-predicted values; (b) mean prediction error (MPE) for bias; and (c) root mean squared error (RMSE) for precision. RESULTS: Overall, all models predicted the mean ΔHbA1c closely, within 0.2% of the observed values for the Phases 2 and 3 studies, at Weeks 26, 36 and 52. All models exhibited little bias (absolute MPE < 0.3%) and comparable precision (RMSE = 0.385-0.507%) estimates. CONCLUSIONS: The transit compartment models performed consistently well for dulaglutide and LY2409021, and therefore, they are preferred for describing glycaemic control for novel antidiabetic compounds with similar mechanisms of action. Fasting glucose is more convenient to measure than average glucose in the clinic setting, favouring the FHH model that utilized fasting glucose as its biomarker.

articles.title: Ocular tolerability of the silica-based intravitreal drug delivery system in the rabbit.
articles.abstract: IIntravitreal therapy has become a cornerstone in the treatment of retinal diseases. Frequent injections challenge patients and healthcare providers, highlighting the need to extend drug action. This has driven the emergence of long-acting, biodegradable carrier systems. Our study evaluated the development, characterization, and tolerability of two silica-based formulations manufactured aseptically: a silica microparticle-hydrogel composite (Si-HGC) and a silica microparticle suspension (Si-MPS). New Zealand White rabbits (n = 32) received intravitreal injections at volumes: Si-HGC (10, 25, and 50 μl) and Si-MPS (50 μl), with 4 rabbits serving as controls. Ocular health was monitored for up to 3 months via intraocular pressure (IOP), slit-lamp examinations, and fundus imaging, while tissue response and material behavior were assessed by histology, immunohistochemistry, proteomics, and silica analysis. Formulations exhibited good ocular tolerability, with no adverse effects. IOP increased transiently post-injection and returned to baseline within 30 minutes. Slit-lamp examination showed no abnormalities, while fundus imaging confirmed volume- and formulation-dependent differences in silica distribution. Histology demonstrated preserved ocular structures, with mild, localized retinal responses near the silica depot, more pronounced at higher volumes. Immunohistochemistry revealed glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) upregulation without consistent evidence of oxidative or protein stress. Proteomic analysis indicated minor, transient changes with a mild inflammatory and oxidative signature that resolved over time. Residual silica analysis confirmed progressive degradation and clearance from the vitreous. Overall, silica-based formulations were developed and showed good handling and reliable performance. Formulations were biocompatible and well-tolerated in eye tissues, offering a promising basis for sustained intravitreal drug delivery.

articles.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: Glutamine contributes to ameliorate inflammation after renal ischemia/reperfusion injury in rats.
Berberine alleviates cobalt chloride-induced neurotoxicity in rats: associated changes in oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and inflammatory signaling markers.
articles.abstract: Cobalt chloride (CoCl2) induces neurotoxicity characterized by chemical hypoxia and oxidative damage, yet protective strategies remain limited. This study investigated the effects of berberine (BBR) against CoCl2-induced neurotoxicity in rats. Male Wistar rats (n = 7 per group) were treated daily for 14 days: control, BBR alone (100 mg/kg), CoCl2 alone (100 mg/kg), and CoCl2 with BBR (50 or 100 mg/kg). CoCl2 reduced central-zone time in the open field and increased latency to the target quadrant in the Morris water maze probe trial, whereas BBR produced only non-significant numerical improvements. CoCl2 disrupted redox homeostasis and altered hippocampal mRNA expression of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress markers, p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK), Janus kinase 3 (JAK3), signal transducer and activator of transcription 5 a (STAT5a), inflammatory mediators, and apoptosis- and autophagy-related genes. BBR improved antioxidant enzyme activities and was accompanied by attenuation of these changes, more strongly at 100 mg/kg. Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) expression recovered at both doses, whereas reductions in heme oxygenase - 1 (HO-1), B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2), protein kinase B beta (AKT2), forkhead box O1 (FOXO1), c-Jun N-terminal kinase 1 (JNK1), and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) were reversed only at 100 mg/kg. Immunohistochemistry indicated that BBR reduced glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and neurofilament light chain (NF-L) immunoreactivity and preserved brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Because gene expression was assessed at the mRNA level, findings are associative and require protein-level validation. BBR co-treatment was associated with reduced CoCl2-induced biochemical, molecular, and histological alterations, but no significant behavioral benefit.

articles.title: Integrative network toxicology, transcriptomic analysis, and experimental validation identify TOP2A-associated molecular alterations in NNK-related hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence implicates nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) in the pathogenesis of various malignancies, yet the biological pathways underlying its effects on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have not been fully elucidated. To characterize the signaling pathways involved in NNK-driven hepatocellular carcinoma, we jointly applied network toxicology, single-cell RNA sequencing, molecular docking, virtual knockout analysis, and in vitro validation. Database mining identified 502 putative NNK-related targets across ChEMBL, CTD, SEA, and SwissTarget, together with 2143 HCC-associated genes retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM, and TTD. Functional enrichment analyses implicated the candidate genes in xenobiotic responses, cell cycle regulation, transcription factor binding, and several cancer-related signaling pathways, particularly the PI3K-Akt, FoxO, and p53 pathways. Following transcriptomic validation in GSE121248 and machine learning prioritization, TOP2A emerged as the leading candidate associated with NNK-related molecular alterations in HCC. TOP2A showed satisfactory discriminatory performance in both GSE121248 and GSE14520, with AUC values exceeding 0.75. Immune cell deconvolution further revealed associations between TOP2A expression and multiple immune cell subsets. In silico gene perturbation analysis identified ORM1 as a candidate gene associated with predicted TOP2A perturbation, suggesting a potential molecular relationship between TOP2A and ORM1 rather than an experimentally established regulatory axis. Subsequent cellular experiments showed that NNK treatment increased growth-related cellular activity and migratory phenotypes in both HuH-7 and Hep 3B2.1-7 cells. NNK exposure was also accompanied by increased TOP2A and ORM1 protein abundance, with consistent western blot findings observed in both HCC cell lines. In summary, this study identifies TOP2A as a potential molecular candidate associated with NNK-related HCC progression and suggests a possible relationship between TOP2A and ORM1 that may contribute to NNK-associated molecular alterations in HCC.

articles.title: Alcohol cue-induced functional connectivity in rats: effects of age of onset and drinking severity.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Adolescents' heightened reward sensitivity has been suggested to contribute to increased risky drinking during this developmental period compared to adulthood. However, little is known about how age of onset and drinking severity relate to alcohol cue-reactivity, a potential biomarker of addiction. OBJECTIVES: The present study investigated alcohol cue-induced functional connectivity in rats defined by age of onset (adolescent or adult) and drinking level (low vs. high; LD vs. HD), following two months of intermittent alcohol exposure. METHODS: Three to six days after alcohol exposure, rats underwent an fMRI olfactory cue-reactivity paradigm, including ethanol, appetitive sugar water and neutral water odour cues. Cue-induced functional connectivity was estimated using trial-wise beta-series correlations. RESULTS: An age effect was observed, with higher medial prefrontal cortex-retrosplenial cortex connectivity for both ethanol > water and ethanol > sugar + water contrasts in adolescent- versus adult-onset rats. However, neither effect met the corrected threshold after adjusting for abstinence duration. No main effects of drinking severity survived correction. However, interactions between age of onset and severity were found. Adolescent-onset HD was associated with reduced prelimbic-anterior cingulate cortex connectivity for ethanol > water compared to LD, while adult-onset LD rats exhibited reduced connectivity compared to adolescent-onset LD rats. Similarly, adolescent-onset HD was associated with reduced amygdala-insula connectivity for ethanol > sugar + water compared to LD and adult-onset HD rats. These interaction effects remained significant after adjusting for abstinence duration. CONCLUSIONS: High adolescent-onset alcohol use was associated with reduced prefrontal and limbic connectivity during alcohol cue exposure. These findings suggest that cue-induced functional connectivity may be sensitive to heavy alcohol exposure during adolescence. While effects may reflect developmental differences, alcohol exposure, or both, they highlight adolescence as a potentially sensitive period for differences in neural cue processing.

articles.title: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis: Current Therapeutic Limitations and a Critical Appraisal of Nanotechnology-based Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) is a neglected parasitic skin infection transmitted by sand flies to humans and remains a major public health challenge in endemic regions with increasing spread into newly affected and previously non-endemic areas. The disease is characterized by disfiguring dermal lesions that can result in prolonged physical, psychological, and socioeconomic impacts. Despite its substantial global burden, therapeutic management of CL remains challenging owing to the absence of effective vaccines, inadequate efficacy and toxicity of currently used drugs, and emergence of drug-resistant Leishmania species. Conventional treatments, including pentavalent antimonials, amphotericin B (AMB), and miltefosine are associated with significant cost, safety, and compliance constraints, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies. This critical review provides an integrated overview of epidemiology, and immunological aspects of CL while highlighting the risk factors contributing to CL spread, such as climate change and political instability. It further critically assesses current treatment strategies and their constraints, underlining the urgent need for safer and more effective alternatives. In this context, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems have been introduced as a rational formulation approach to overcome the biopharmaceutical and pharmacokinetic challenges associated with current and emerging antileishmanial agents. Nano formulations such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles and metallic nanostructures have revealed promising preclinical results for CL. This review investigates the potential of nano-based formulations to guide and support the future development of enhanced treatment strategies for CL. Despite advancements in nanotechnology research, translational obstacles persist, including scalability, cost-efficiency and regulatory approval. Nevertheless, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems represent a promising approach to improve the efficacy, targeting and safety profile of antileishmanial therapies, although further translational and clinical studies are required before their widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Informing Ambulatory Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Study Design Using Models Bridging Timed Function Tests and Fat Fraction Imaging Biomarkers.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to inform the use of magnetic resonance (MR) imaging biomarkers in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) clinical trials by quantifying longitudinal associations between timed function tests (TFTs) (i.e., the 10-m walk/run (TMW), supine-to-stand (STS), and climb 4 stairs (CFS)) and fat fraction (FF) measures from two leg muscles (i.e., the soleus (SOL) and vastus lateralis (VL)). Additionally, this study aimed to identify sensitive age ranges and clinically relevant covariate effects for these measures. Six multivariate disease progression models were developed using natural history data from the ImagingNMD study (NCT01484678) and validated with data from investigational clinical trials, employing Bayesian nonlinear mixed-effects modeling in Monolix (ver. 2023R1). A sigmoid Emax function and a multiplication of Chapman-Richards growth and sigmoid Imax function best captured the longitudinal dynamics of FF and TFT measures, respectively. The population distributions of the simulated ages at which the measures reach half of their maximum change (  DPT 50   ), peaked at 12.8, 10.6, and 11.4 years for TMW, STS, and CFS velocity, respectively, and 12.4 and 10.9 years for FF-SOL and FF-VL. Steroid use delayed  DPT 50   of STS and CFS velocities and FF-SOL. Baseline endpoint values robustly predicted individualized trajectories for STS velocity (for all ages) and FF-VL (in older baseline age groups), but not for other measures. Older baseline age groups showed consistent  DPT 50   predictions across models. The established multivariate models can serve as informative tools for biomarker selection and refinement of inclusion/exclusion criteria in DMD clinical trials.

articles.title: Microdosing Approach for Switching From Methadone to Buprenorphine in Opioid Disorder: A French Case Series.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Switching from methadone to buprenorphine remains challenging because conventional induction often requires methadone reduction and cessation and the onset of opioid withdrawal.
