The microdosing approach allows for the gradual introduction of buprenorphine while methadone dosing is maintained. Despite growing evidence supporting this approach, published experience remains limited, particularly in French outpatient settings. MATERIAL AND METHODS: We report the first French case series of methadone-to-buprenorphine transfers using microdosing in routine clinical practice, predominantly in an outpatient setting. We retrospectively reviewed all patients who underwent methadone-to-buprenorphine transfer using a 14-day microdosing approach at two specialist addiction treatment centers in Lyon, France, between March and June 2026. The protocol was adapted from published Australian protocols to formulations available in France. Data on opioid doses, withdrawal symptoms, adverse events, adherence and treatment outcomes were collected from medical records. RESULTS: Ten patients (8 men, 2 women) underwent the protocol. Nine transfers were performed as outpatients and one during hospitalization. Six patients (60%) successfully completed the transition, including five outpatients. Withdrawal symptoms were absent or mild among successful transfers. Two patients discontinued the protocol because of withdrawal symptoms, whereas two were lost to follow-up. No severe adverse events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: This first French case series, mainly outpatient, found that methadone-to-buprenorphine transfer using a 14-day microdosing protocol was feasible, with a 60% completion rate. Microdosing may offer a practical outpatient option and reduce healthcare costs versus inpatient hospitalization. Larger prospective studies using standardized withdrawal scales are needed to confirm these findings and assess feasibility and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Integrating Inflammation, Pathway Modulation, and Circadian Clock Genes: Conventional and Phytochemical Strategies for Safer Osteoporosis Therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Osteoporosis is a systemic and silent bone disease that destroys bone microarchitecture, thereby increasing the risk of bone fracture, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Although it is usually considered a structural deficit, bone remodeling is now fundamentally dependent on the circadian clock, osteoblast cells (responsible for the formation of new bone tissues), osteoclast cells (responsible for breaking down bone tissues), and hormonal rhythms, such as cortisol, melatonin, growth hormone, and parathyroid hormones. METHODS: Current treatment methods for osteoporosis do not fully restore bone quality and cause many side effects. To address these problems, recent studies have suggested that phytomolecules, as promising therapeutic candidates, can be used for treatment. The use of phytomolecules in combination with conventional treatment, in a time-sensitive manner aligned with circadian biology, is expected to be a better treatment for osteoporosis. RESULTS: Disturbances in the sleep-wake cycle or in neurotransmitter homeostasis dysregulate core clock genes (BMAL-1, CLOCK, PER, CRY) in bone cells, causing instability in bone turnover. Osteochronotherapy involves scheduling the intake of conventional drugs and phytochemicals in accordance with the circadian rhythms of bone cells. This chronobiological method aims to achieve the highest therapeutic efficacy and the lowest toxicity, representing an advanced approach to osteoporosis treatment. In vitro studies have shown that bioactive agents, mainly resveratrol, icariin, genistein, quercetin, and baicalein, have osteoprotective activities with multimodal actions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and direct effects on RANKL/OPG, AMPK/SIRT1, ESR, NF-κB, and Wnt/β-catenin. DISCUSSION: The study highlights the importance of incorporating circadian biology into osteoporosis management. The synchronization of therapies with the biological clock can maximize efficiency, reduce adverse effects, and help develop a new approach to bone health. The results emphasize the importance of using phytochemicals as an adjunct therapy, shed light on knowledge gaps in bone remodeling, and suggest possible avenues for utilizing circadian regulation of osteoblasts and osteoclasts to enhance bone density. Furthermore, the incorporation of natural compounds with chronotherapy represents a paradigm shift toward more personalized, safer, and biologically harmonized strategies for osteoporosis therapy. These insights also highlight critical knowledge gaps in bone remodeling research, encouraging future studies to explore how circadian rhythms and neurotransmitter pathways can be leveraged to advance precision medicine in skeletal health. CONCLUSION: It is now evident that circadian rhythm serves as an important mediator for the maintenance of healthy bones because of its function in bone remodeling. In future research, emphasis must also be placed on exploring the possible differential regulation of osteoclasts and osteoblasts by various circadian rhythms and how such regulation can help enhance bone strength. The review concludes by examining the interplay among neurotransmitter pathways, circadian biology, and sleep quality in relation to conventional and phytochemical interventions.

articles.title: Unraveling the Molecular Landscape of Sarcopenia: Pathophysiology, Omics Integration, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies for Healthy Aging.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia, the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and functional capacity with advancing age, poses a critical public health burden in older populations, significantly increasing the risk of disability, morbidity, and mortality. Sarcopenia is a complex condition influenced by numerous systemic and metabolic factors involving multiple pathophysiological processes that result in altered skeletal muscle protein metabolism, reduced production and activity of anabolic hormones, chronic inflammation, and impaired muscle coordination, endurance, and physical performance, as well as mitochondrial dysfunction. Recent advances in molecular biology and biomechanics provide the scientific community with tools to investigate the physiological processes and cellular mechanisms driving the development of sarcopenia. The literature highlights that multiple molecular mechanisms contribute to the genetic susceptibility to sarcopenia, and individuals with sarcopenia can be more effectively evaluated and monitored using emerging diagnostic tests based on omics technologies, including genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, than conventional approaches, thereby facilitating earlier diagnosis and more targeted treatment. Interventions for the management of sarcopenia may include optimizing nutrition, promoting physical activity and structured exercise, using novel pharmacological therapies, including myostatin inhibitors and selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs), and advancing public health policies focused on sarcopenia awareness, screening, and education. Sarcopenia significantly compromises quality of life and contributes to elevated morbidity and mortality rates in older adults.

articles.title: Phytoconstituents in Alopecia: Molecular Evidence, Preclinical Potential, and Emerging Delivery Strategies.
articles.abstract: Alopecia is a multifactorial dermatological disorder characterized by partial or complete hair loss, significantly affecting patients' quality of life and psychological well-being. Although conventional therapies, including minoxidil and finasteride, remain the standard treatment options, their clinical efficacy is often limited by variable therapeutic responses, adverse effects, and the need for prolonged use. Consequently, there is growing interest in identifying safer and more effective therapeutic alternatives. Phytoconstituents derived from medicinal plants have emerged as promising candidates owing to their multi-target pharmacological activities and favorable safety profiles. This review comprehensively summarizes the therapeutic potential of plant-derived bioactive compounds in alopecia management, highlighting their underlying molecular mechanisms. Major classes of phytochemicals, including flavonoids, terpenoids, alkaloids, saponins, and phenolic compounds, exhibit significant hair growth-promoting properties through multiple pathways, such as inhibition of 5α-reductase, attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammation, modulation of growth factors, stimulation of dermal papilla cell proliferation, and activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Evidence from in vitro, in vivo, and a limited number of clinical studies supports the efficacy of these natural compounds in promoting hair follicle regeneration and delaying hair loss. Furthermore, recent advances in nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems have improved the stability, bioavailability, and targeted delivery of phytoconstituents, while emerging regenerative strategies, including stem cell- and gene-based therapies, offer additional opportunities for enhancing treatment outcomes. Despite encouraging preclinical findings, clinical translation remains constrained by insufficient standardization, limited high-quality clinical evidence, and regulatory challenges. Evidence from in vitro and animal studies indicates that several plant-derived compounds can modulate biological processes relevant to hair-follicle function, including androgen metabolism, oxidative stress, inflammation, growth-factor signalling, and Wnt/β-catenin-associated pathways. However, the strength of mechanistic evidence varies considerably, and pathway modulation should not be equated with demonstration of direct molecular target engagement. Human evidence remains limited, with small and heterogeneous clinical studies and insufficient high-quality randomized controlled trials for most phytoconstituents. Emerging follicle-targeted delivery systems, including lipid-based nanocarriers, vesicular systems, and microneedle-assisted approaches, may improve local exposure, but their clinical translation remains at an early stage. Overall, current evidence supports the preclinical promise of selected phytoconstituents rather than establishing them as a clinically validated therapeutic strategy for alopecia. Future studies should prioritize standardized phytochemical characterization, direct target identification, follicular pharmacokinetics, rigorous safety assessment, and well-designed controlled clinical trials.

articles.title: Investigating the effect of simultaneous administration of liposomal nano-carriers containing methotrexate and curcumin on KG-1 leukemia cells.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is the most common form of acute leukemia among adults, accounting for about one-third of all diagnosed cases of leukemia. Its incidence tends to increase with age. AML accounts for close to one-third of all leukemia diagnoses. Liposomes are nano-carriers that can improve the cellular uptake of drugs and genes. Methotrexate functions as an anti-folate medication, exhibiting both anti-cancer and immune-suppressing properties. Additionally, it possesses a diverse array of biological characteristics, including anti-inflammatory and anti-proliferative effects. Curcumin (CUR) is a polyphenol extracted from the rhizomes of Curcuma longa (Turmeric) and has gained worldwide attention because of its anticancer, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant characteristics. Conventional cancer therapies (chemotherapy) cannot precisely target the cancerous cells without affecting the healthy ones. Various factors affect the development and use of effective cancer drugs. Thus nano-carriers can help us deliver the drug to the exactly targeted organ and reduce the side effects on other healthy cells and organs. This research aims to investigate the therapeutic efficacy of combining liposomal Methotrexate and Curcumin in treating KG-1 cancer cells. METHODS: Drug-loaded liposomes were formulated using the thin-film hydration technique, followed by a series of analyses including size and zeta potential measurements, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM), encapsulation efficiency assessment, and in vitro drug release studies. Additionally, the cellular uptake of the drugs and their cytotoxicity were evaluated using the MTT assay. RESULTS: All of the performed characterizations had suitable results. The liposome size was about 90 nm and the zeta potential was negative. The entrapment efficiency of Methotrexate (MTX) and CUR in nanoliposome was high and the MTX and CUR-loaded nanoliposome released MTX and CUR within 72 h with the capability of an accelerated release in an acidic milieu. CONCLUSION: Consequently, the liposomal formulation of CUR and MTX exhibited higher toxicity compared to their free-form combination. Moreover, the internalization of MTX and CUR nanoliposomes into human KG-1 cells in vitro was observed.

articles.title: Cigarette smoke exposure upregulates peripheral blood mRNA levels of ITGA2B, TIMP1, JAK2, and STAT3 and increases platelet count in rats: implications for the thrombocytosis and ET-related molecular alterations.
articles.abstract: To investigate cigarette smoke exposure as an environmental risk factor in Essential Thrombocythemia(ET) and validate key regulated target genes, we integrated peripheral blood transcriptomic data from ET patients with the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database(CTD) to screen for Environmental pollutants(EPs) and target genes. Key genes were identified via protein-protein interaction(PPI) network analysis, and their binding affinities with Nicotine, a component of cigarette smoke, were simulated through molecular docking. An 8-week cigarette smoke exposure model was established in SD rats to monitor dynamic changes in target gene mRNA expression(qRT-PCR) and platelet counts. Bioinformatics analysis identified 558 differentially expressed genes and 17 EPs, highlighting Nicotine and reactive oxygen species(ROS) as crucial factors. Molecular docking revealed strong binding between Nicotine and ITGA2B(-6.7 kcal/mol) and TIMP1(-6.0 kcal/mol). In rats, cigarette smoke exposure significantly upregulated ITGA2B, TIMP1(from week 6, p < 0.05) and JAK2, STAT3(from week 4, p < 0.05), which correlated with increased platelet counts (p = 0.041). Our study demonstrated that cigarette smoke exposure induced platelet proliferation mediated by ITGA2B and TIMP1. Furthermore, the upregulation of JAK2 and STAT3 might be associated with excessive platelet production. These findings suggest that controlling cigarette smoke exposure might be useful in preventing thrombocytosis both in healthy and ET subjects.

articles.title: Neuroprotective role of hesperidin against aluminium-induced neurotoxicity: evidence from behavioural changes and suppression of inflammatory and oxidative markers.
articles.abstract: Chronic aluminium exposure is an established environmental risk factor for cognitive decline, acting largely through oxidative injury and glial-driven inflammation in the brain. Hesperidin, a citrus flavanone glycoside with reported antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity, was examined for protection against aluminium chloride (AlCl₃) neurotoxicity. Male Swiss albino mice (n = 5 per group) received AlCl₃ alone or AlCl₃ together with hesperidin at 50 or 100 mg/kg by oral gavage for 28 days, alongside a vehicle-treated control. Spatial working memory and exploratory behaviour were assessed using the Y-maze and open field tests, and brain tissue was analysed for superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, glutathione S-transferase (GST), malondialdehyde (MDA), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α). AlCl₃ produced consistent behavioural impairment, with reduced rearing and line crossing, prolonged centre-square duration, and a fall in correct Y-maze alternation by day 28 compared to control (p < 0.05). Total arm entries were not significantly reduced by AlCl₃, indicating that the alternation deficit did not reflect altered exploratory activity. These deficits were accompanied by depleted SOD, catalase, and GST activity, elevated MDA, and pronounced increases in IL-1β and TNF-α. Hesperidin reversed this profile in a dose-related manner. The 100 mg/kg dose significantly restored line crossing and Y-maze alternation, shortened centre-square duration, raised antioxidant enzyme activity, lowered lipid peroxidation, and suppressed both cytokines compared to the AlCl₃-only group (p < 0.05), while the lower dose produced intermediate effects. These findings indicate that hesperidin protects the mouse brain against aluminium-induced cognitive and biochemical damage, with behavioural recovery accompanied by reinforcement of endogenous antioxidant enzyme activity and reduction of pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. The upstream signalling responsible was not measured in this study, and the findings support further preclinical evaluation rather than any claim of therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Integration of multi-omics and network toxicology suggests potential mechanisms linking artificial sweeteners to chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial sweeteners (AS) are widely consumed as sugar substitutes. However, their potential involvement in the pathogenesis of chronic kidney disease (CKD) presents a complex toxicological question. This study aims to explore the potential molecular mechanisms and "toxicant-target-disease" interactions that may link AS exposure to renal function decline. METHODS: We suggested a systems toxicology framework integrating network pharmacology, ensemble machine learning, and multi-dimensional bioinformatics. Nine machine learning algorithms were applied to human CKD transcriptomic datasets (GEO) to screen for diagnostic markers. The findings were further evaluated via immune infiltration profiling, molecular docking simulations, and Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. RESULTS: Network analysis identified 448 convergent targets bridging AS exposure to CKD, which were enriched in PI3K-AKT signaling and inflammatory cascades. Machine learning prioritized five core toxicological effectors: MAP2K1, IKBKB, CASP1, IL1B and TLR2. These biomarkers exhibited high diagnostic potential and correlated with dysregulated renal immune microenvironments, notably involving monocyte and mast cell infiltration. Molecular docking predicted stable binding affinities between AS components and these targets, while MR analyses provided genetic evidence supporting a potential causal effect of specific target IL1B on CKD risk. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings propose a multi-layered mechanism wherein artificial sweeteners may exacerbate renal decline, potentially via inflammasome-mediated and innate immune pathways. This study offers a theoretical foundation for further safety re-evaluation of sugar substitutes and identifies a candidate biomarker panel for CKD risk assessment.

articles.title: Quality by Design-Assisted Development of Ticagrelor Nanocrystals to Enhance Dissolution Performance and Bioavailability.
articles.abstract: Poor aqueous solubility remains a major limitation in the oral delivery of ticagrelor (TCG). The aim of this study was to develop and systematically optimize TCG nanosuspensions using a Quality by Design (QbD) framework and translate the optimized formulation into a solid dosage form with improved in-vivo performance. A rotatable central composite design was employed to investigate the effects of critical formulation and process parameters on particle size, polydispersity index, and zeta potential. The optimized nanosuspension was converted into a solid intermediate by freeze-drying, followed by physicochemical characterization using X-Ray Powder Diffraction (XRPD), and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). The dried nanocrystals were further processed into film-coated tablets and evaluated for dissolution and pharmacokinetic performance. The QbD approach enabled identification of significant parameter interactions and establishment of a predictive design space. They optimized nanocrystal formulation with a particle size value of 244 nm ± 0.01 resulted in a fivefold increase in dissolution rate, and approximately 2.5 fold enhancement in Cmax as well as AUC0-24 compared to the Brilinta® film-coated tablets. This study presents an integrated development strategy linking nanosuspension engineering, conversion of optimized nanosuspension into a solid dosage form and in-vivo validation to improve the oral bioavailability of poorly soluble drugs. Long term stability data for film coated tablets comprising dried nanocrystals, demonstrated acceptable stability under long-term storage conditions; however, limitations were observed under accelerated storage conditions and show the feasibility of using freeze drying as a processing method to convert a nanosuspension into a solid dosage form with improved in-vivo exposure compared to the commercial formulation.

articles.title: Aggregation-Caused Quenching (ACQ)-Based Fluorescence Tracing Reveals Ileum-Biased Absorption of Paeoniflorin from Glycyrrhiza Protein Nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Paeoniflorin (PF) is a hydrophilic natural product with limited oral bioavailability, primarily due to poor intestinal permeability. Glycyrrhiza protein-based self-assembling nanocarriers were used for PF encapsulation, resulting in the formation of Glycyrrhiza protein-paeoniflorin nanoparticles (GP-PF NPs), which have previously been shown to improve systemic exposure to PF; however, their gastrointestinal fate and segment-dependent absorption behavior remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, GP-PF NPs were evaluated as an oral protein-based delivery system using physicochemical characterization, simulated gastrointestinal stability assessment, aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ)-based fluorescence tracing, single-pass intestinal perfusion, and Peyer's patch-focused immunofluorescence imaging. Reproducible nanoscale properties were observed for GP-PF NPs, and particulate characteristics were maintained under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. After oral administration, sequential transit of P2-labeled GP-PF NP-associated fluorescence from the duodenum to the jejunum and ileum was observed, with signal attenuation occurring within 8 h. In single-pass intestinal perfusion studies, the apparent permeability coefficient and absorption rate constant of PF were significantly increased by GP-PF NPs in the ileum, whereas no significant enhancement was observed in the duodenum or jejunum. Higher accumulation of FITC-labeled GP-PF NPs was observed in ileal Peyer's patch regions than in adjacent non-Peyer's patch regions, and spatial association with GP2-positive areas was identified. Region-dependent enhancement of PF absorption by GP-PF NPs was therefore indicated, with preferential enhancement in the ileum potentially associated with Peyer's patch-related localization. Biopharmaceutical insights into the rational design of protein-based oral nanocarriers for poorly permeable hydrophilic compounds are provided by these findings.

articles.title: Investigation of the effects of protocatechuic acid and its nanostructured lipid carrier formulation on lipopolysaccharide-induced systemic inflammation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Protocatechuic acid (PCA) exhibits promising antiinflammatory and neuroprotective properties; however, its therapeutic application is limited by rapid metabolism and poor bioavailability. PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop a Nanostructured Lipid Carrier (NLC) formulation of PCA as a potential strategy to improve its delivery and to evaluate its efficacy against free PCA in a murine model of neuroinflammation. METHODS: Adult male BALB/c mice received either free PCA or the nanostructured lipid carrier formulation of PCA (NLCPCA) (75 mg/kg, i.p.) for seven days prior to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) administration (0.83 mg/kg). Behavioural outcomes were assessed using the tail suspension test (depression-related behaviour), light-dark box and hole-board tests (anxiety-like behaviour), and the open-field test (locomotor activity). Subsequently, molecular analyses were conducted to delineate the relationship between neuroinflammation and affective behaviours. RESULTS: LPS administration did not produce a robust depressive-like phenotype in the tail suspension test, whereas anxiety-related measures were consistently impaired across behavioural paradigms. Free PCA failed to reverse LPS-induced cytokine elevations and, in the LPS-challenged animals, even exhibited a paradoxical proinflammatory profile. In contrast, ​NLCPCA​ effectively ameliorated LPS-induced anxiety-like behaviours and significantly suppressed TLR4/NF-κB-associated neuroinflammatory signaling. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that the therapeutic efficacy of PCA is highly formulation-dependent, suggesting that nanoencapsulation may help to overcome the limitations of the free compound. In conclusion, NLCPCA, but not free PCA, emerges as a promising anti​inflammatory and anxiolytic candidate for inflammation-related neuropsychiatric disorders.

articles.title: Prediction of extended clearance pathways (renal, hepatic metabolism and hepatic transporter uptake) in small molecules using structural and physicochemical descriptors.
articles.abstract: Prediction of the predominant rate-determining drug clearance pathway remains an important challenge during the early stages of drug development. Computational modelling approaches provide a practical strategy for predicting clearance behaviour of pharmacokinetic properties.This study developed binary logistic regression, artificial neural-network models, and random forest models to predict rate-determining drug clearance pathways within the framework of the Extended Clearance Classification System (ECCS).A two-stage classification strategy was implemented. In Stage 1, compounds were classified as hepatic uptake or non-uptake compounds, whereas Stage 2 distinguished renal excretion from hepatic metabolism among the remaining compounds. Logistic regression, artificial neural network and random forest approaches were evaluated for each classification stage using test sets.The results indicate that calculated molecular structural and physicochemical descriptors can provide useful information for clearance pathway prediction without requiring experimentally determined permeability measurements. The best-performing approach depended on the classification task: random forest achieved the highest overall accuracy in Stage 1, whereas logistic regression and the neural network outperformed random forest in Stage 2. Overall, the results indicate that molecular structural and physicochemical descriptors alone can provide useful information for clearance pathway prediction.

articles.title: Association Between Dupilumab and Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases Among US Patients With COPD: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity. Although dupilumab reduces COPD exacerbations, its cardiovascular effects remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between dupilumab and cardiovascular disease risk among patients with COPD. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the US TriNetX electronic health records database with a new-user design. Patients aged ≥40 years with COPD between October 1, 2024, and June 1, 2025, receiving triple inhaler therapy were included. Patients initiating dupilumab within 30 days after COPD exacerbation were compared with those receiving triple inhaler therapy. Outcomes included acute myocardial infarction (AMI), cerebral infarction, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation/flutter (AFib/AFl). Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to balance covariates. Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Among 72 113 patients with COPD, 1352 matched pairs were analyzed. Dupilumab was associated with increased risks of heart failure (HR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.44-2.08) and AFib/AFl (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.24-1.99) compared with triple inhaler therapy. No associations were observed for AMI (HR, 1.38; 95% CI, 0.92-2.06) and cerebral infarction (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.48-1.45). Associations with heart failure and AFib/AFl remained consistent across sensitivity analyses and were observed in both eosinophil subgroups. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Higher rates of heart failure and AFib/AFl were observed among dupilumab initiators than patients receiving triple inhaler therapy alone. Given the residual confounding, these findings do not establish a causal cardiovascular effect of dupilumab. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.
